papers.title: Sleep Duration Phenotypes and Dynamic Homeostasis: A Wave-Model Framework.
papers.summary: Across 105 baseline 8-h and 420 extended 14-h nights in 15 individuals, sleep duration and NREM intensity behaved as largely independent traits, each predicting its own expression but not the companion trait. The authors interpret these findings via a wave model in which sleep duration reflects sleep-cycle geometry (stability-landscape width) and NREM intensity reflects oscillation amplitude and homeostatic deviation.

papers.title: Cross-Band Coupling of EEG Infraslow Oscillations during NREM Sleep in Mice.
papers.summary: Analyzed cross-band coupling of EEG infraslow oscillations (0.01–0.03 Hz) across six frequency bands during NREM sleep in wild-type and LepR-Cre mice, finding that alpha, sigma, beta, and theta ISOs form a strongly correlated and phase-locked motif replicated across genotypes. ISOs were weak in gamma and absent in delta, suggesting a coupled minute-scale organization principle of sleep microstructures.

papers.title: Lifespan Trajectories of Resting State Bipolar EEG Power.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Derived normative lifespan trajectories of resting-state bipolar EEG power from 12,906 observations in 5,781 participants aged 12-70 without alcohol use disorder, across seven frequency bands and 24 bipolar channels. Power sharply decreased from age 12 to the early 20s, followed by divergent patterns including beta increases and mixed theta/alpha changes, with striking sex differences in inter-frequency correlation trajectories.

papers.title: NREM sleep microarchitecture is associated with internalizing symptoms and emotional functioning in early adolescence.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Examined NREM sleep oscillations using automated slow oscillation and spindle detection in 9–13-year-olds with anxiety disorders (n=17) versus non-psychiatric comparisons (n=26), alongside an emotional processing task and parent-reported mental health measures. Shorter slow spindle duration was found in the anxiety group and, across the sample, was associated with greater internalizing symptoms and emotional arousal/look-away behavior.

papers.title: REM sleep infraslow rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptom severity.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Examined REM infraslow (~0.01 Hz) rhythms against neuropsychiatric symptom scores in a cross-sectional polysomnographic dataset of 59 male veterans. Higher infraslow respiratory rate frequencies correlated with multiple symptoms (PTSD, pain, anxiety, depression, cognitive difficulties), whereas conventional REM metrics showed no significant correlations.

papers.title: Brief Trains of Closed-loop TMS Induce Controllable Power in FM-theta Oscillations.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In six healthy adults performing a working memory task, four-pulse 6 Hz TMS trains locked to real-time frontal-midline theta troughs versus peaks produced phase-dependent modulation of post-train FM-theta power. Trough-triggered trains transiently increased total (4.6-7.1 Hz) and induced (5.0-7.8 Hz) theta power roughly 50-440 ms after stimulation, without effects on task performance or evoked power.

papers.title: Phase-dependent EEG decoding of continuous visual stimuli.
papers.summary: Using a phase-dependent decoding approach on EEG recorded while participants viewed 2-second Gabor patches, stimulus decoding accuracy varied systematically with alpha phase, following a smooth unimodal profile peaking over occipito-parietal electrodes. The effects emerged well after stimulus onset and generalized to earlier time points, indicating visual information is represented more accurately at specific alpha phases during continuous input.

papers.title: Mechanisms of auditory cortex injury and the protective effects of reoxygenation in a rat model of intermittent hypoxia.
papers.summary: Used a rat intermittent hypoxia model to examine auditory cortical injury and recovery after one week of normoxic reoxygenation. Intermittent hypoxia caused high-frequency hearing loss and increased spontaneous firing in primary auditory cortex that reversed with reoxygenation, while GABA and serotonin rose after recovery and redox, inflammatory, and metabolomic abnormalities recovered asynchronously, with some persisting.

papers.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Designed and tested three 3D-printed hair-anchored EEG electrode attachments for Type 4a-4c Afro-textured hairstyles in 17 healthy adults, compared with conventional cap electrodes during resting and walking trials. Novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance, cut disconnection from 20% to 0.1%, and improved signal quality (peak alpha power and 1/f component) without differing comfort.

papers.title: Compensatory drive and sleep-related phantom limb pain: the moderating role of autonomic reserve.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In 121 amputee adults, poorer sleep was associated with greater phantom limb and residual limb pain, and a sleep × autonomic reserve × autonomic drive interaction moderated phantom limb pain (b = -0.51, p = 0.026), with the strongest sleep-pain association under high drive with reduced reserve. No single HRV index moderated the associations.

papers.title: Skin-Interfaced Flexible Sensors for Continuous Monitoring of Thermal, Mechanical, Electrical, and Respiratory Signals.
papers.summary: This review examines how physiological information from skin-interfaced flexible sensors is preserved or altered across the skin-device interface, sensor response, and signal interpretation for temperature, mechanical, biopotential, electrodermal, and respiratory monitoring. It emphasizes that major limitations arise from interface conditions and environmental/mechanical interference and that reliable monitoring requires reference-based validation of the claimed physiological output.

papers.title: A Complementary Dual-Branch Receptive Field Network for Cross-Channel-Density Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: The authors propose DBRFNet, a complementary dual-branch receptive field network with multi-scale temporal branches and progressive spatio-temporal modules for cross-channel-density motor imagery EEG decoding. It achieved accuracies of 80.48%, 84.37%, and 92.24% under cross-validation on low-, medium-, and high-density public datasets, with ablation studies supporting each architectural component.

papers.title: The Raine Study: a multigenerational Western Australian birth and life-course cohort advancing research on the developmental origins of health and disease.
papers.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
papers.summary: This paper describes the Raine Study, a Western Australian multigenerational pregnancy cohort established in 1989 with 2900 pregnant women and 2868 live births, now recruiting Generation 3. It reports the cohort's evolution into a life-course resource whose findings have informed clinical guidelines and health policy across prenatal care, neurodevelopment, cardiometabolic health, mental health, sleep, and assisted reproductive technologies.

papers.title: Longitudinal Imaging in a Mouse Model of Focal Cortical Dysplasia Reveals Lesion Expansion and Loss of Pre-Discharge Neuronal Recruitment
papers.summary: Using chronic cranial window two-photon calcium imaging and video-EEG in a mouse model of focal cortical dysplasia type II with the mTOR p.L2427P variant, the authors found progressive lesion expansion in adulthood, partly from somatic growth of dysmorphic neurons. Dysmorphic and pyramidal cell activity declined in seizing mice, and pre-discharge neuronal recruitment in lesional cortex weakened by late disease stages.

papers.title: Integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, and cognitive function in obstructive sleep apnea: A pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory pilot study integrated driving-simulator performance, eye tracking, Psychomotor Vigilance Test, and CANTAB cognitive testing in patients with suspected OSA, finding baseline single-task simulator reaction time correlated with apnea severity and multitask accuracy with nocturnal hypoxemia (T90). After 6-12 months of CPAP, simple reaction times improved in both the simulator and PVT, while multitasking and CANTAB measures did not change significantly.

papers.title: Circadian-Based Optimization of Pharmacotherapy in Chronic Diseases: Integrating Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Disease Rhythm.
papers.summary: This review integrates chronopharmacology and chronotherapy to examine how circadian rhythms affect pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and disease activity in chronic conditions, with examples such as evening statin dosing, timed bronchodilators, and modified-release glucocorticoids. It concludes that circadian-timed therapy can improve efficacy and reduce toxicity, but evidence is variable and some strategies (e.g., bedtime antihypertensive dosing) show conflicting trial results.

papers.title: Assessment of Sleep Quality and Modifiable Disruptors in Postoperative Paediatric Patients: A Clinical Audit.
papers.summary: A clinical audit of 19 postoperative paediatric inpatients assessed sleep quality and modifiable disruptors, finding fair sleep in 8/14 children in multi-bed bays and over five overnight awakenings in 6/14. Nursing observations (71.4% bays, 80.0% cubicles) and pain (52.6% overall) were the most reported contributors, and only 36.8% of families were asked about sleep needs.

papers.title: Circadian and Sex-Specific Responses to Alternaria alternata in Allergic Airway Inflammation.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a preclinical mouse model, Alternaria alternata exposure induced allergic airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and epithelial barrier disruption in a circadian- and sex-dependent manner, with females showing stronger inflammation at ZT0 and males at ZT12. Peak inflammation coincided with enhanced STAT1/STAT3/STAT6 activation and altered core clock protein expression, supporting chronotherapeutic approaches for asthma.

papers.title: Biological Mechanisms Underlying the Adverse Health Consequences of Human Circadian Misalignment from Night Shift Work.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes human evidence on biological mechanisms linking night-shift-work circadian misalignment to adverse health, describing central-peripheral rhythm uncoupling reflected in exosomal cargo and gut-microbiome mediation. Internal desynchrony is linked to insulin resistance, cardiometabolic and immune perturbation, mental health erosion, and mistimed DNA repair that may promote genomic instability and carcinogenesis; time-restricted eating is proposed for metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Why sleep assessment belongs in the memory clinic.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This Perspective argues that sleep disturbances (insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, circadian disruption, REM sleep behavior disorder) are highly prevalent in memory-clinic populations and linked to cognitive decline and neurodegeneration, yet are not routinely assessed. It compares sleep assessment approaches across four international contexts and proposes a pragmatic stepped-care framework for screening, referral, and personalized management.

papers.title: Chronotherapy for retinopathy: Unraveling the mystery of Rev-erbα in the circadian rhythm.
papers.summary: This review examines circadian disruption in retinal disease, reporting that Rev-erbα and melanopsin form an antagonistic retinal system regulating intraocular dopamine-melatonin rhythm and homeostasis. Disruption of this system is linked to oxidative stress, inflammation, and emotional dysregulation, and chronotherapy is proposed as a promising intervention for circadian-misalignment-associated retinopathies.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture Combined with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia Alleviates Insomnia-Anxiety Comorbidity in Gynecological Cancer Patients Undergoing Chemotherapy: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 76 gynecological cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, adding electroacupuncture to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia produced greater reductions in PSQI global score (mean difference -3.11, 95% CI -4.11 to -2.11) and higher rates of AIS ≤6 (71.1% vs 42.1%) and HAMA ≤14 (92.1% vs 65.8%) than sham EA plus CBT-I. Deep sleep, REM sleep, sleep score, and overall response rate were also higher with EA, with no serious adverse events.

papers.title: Cerebellar Continuous Theta Burst Stimulation for Insomnia Disorder: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized sham-controlled trial of 72 patients with insomnia disorder, 2 weeks of cerebellar continuous theta burst stimulation produced a ≥3-point PSQI improvement in 75.0% versus 33.3% with sham (adjusted OR 6.06, 95% CI 2.17-18.50) and reduced PSQI scores at post-treatment and 1 month. Insomnia Severity Index, Hamilton Anxiety Scale, and Hamilton Depression Scale also improved, with no serious adverse events.

papers.title: Circadian misalignment associates with inflammation, gut barrier, and microbiome composition in humans with obesity.
papers.summary: In 87 adults with obesity from a randomized clinical trial, late chronotype was associated with greater metabolic syndrome burden, and circadian misalignment was associated with increased gut permeability and metabolic inflammation, an association stronger among participants with higher permeability. These patterns co-occurred with lower abundance of short-chain fatty acid-associated bacteria, and intervention-related permeability changes corresponded with changes in these taxa.

papers.title: Bipolar Disorder and Epilepsy: Clinical and Neurobiological Overlaps, Evidence Gaps, and an Exploratory Systems Perspective.
papers.summary: This narrative review examined genetic, neuroimaging, cognitive, neuroplasticity, neuroinflammatory, stress-biology, network, and treatment-response evidence for overlap between bipolar disorder and epilepsy, finding partially overlapping features such as altered excitation-inhibition balance and large-scale network abnormalities. The authors conclude that shared causal mechanisms are not yet established and propose an integrative network-neuroplasticity framework as a heuristic for future longitudinal and comparative studies.

papers.title: Finding rhythm: Individualizing the timing of home nutrition support.
papers.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
papers.summary: This clinical review discusses individualizing the timing of home nutrition support infusions, contrasting standard overnight cyclic regimens with daytime infusions that may better align with circadian rhythms and improve sleep quality. It recommends a patient-centered approach balancing clinical goals, quality of life, psychosocial factors, sleep, routines, and safety, with ongoing interdisciplinary reassessment of infusion schedules.

papers.title: Coping-Strategies as a Mediator Between Symptoms of Sleeping Problems and Risk of Suicide.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional online survey of 1014 adults, sleep-related symptoms were positively associated with suicide risk, and multiple mediation analysis showed negative self-focus was the strongest mediating coping strategy, while positive reappraisal and seeking social support were protective mediators. A significant direct effect remained, indicating partial mediation.

papers.title: Bridging the gap: advanced chromatin biotechnologies for circadian epigenomic profiling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
keywords: head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
papers.summary: This review examines chromatin-based biotechnologies—chromatin conformation capture, ChIP, DNA methylation profiling, ATAC-seq, and single-cell approaches—for dissecting circadian clock disruption and identifying epigenomic biomarkers in HNSCC. It proposes integrating these assays across HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors to test whether circadian dysregulation reflects transcriptional deregulation alone or structural genome remodeling driving progression and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: Late Sleep Timing is Associated with Metabolic Risk in Postmenopausal Women.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In 122 postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity, a cross-sectional study using seven days of actigraphy, sleep logs, and text-message food timing data found that later sleep onset was associated with greater visceral adipose tissue, but not insulin resistance, blood pressure, or triglycerides. A random-forest model identified sleep onset time, sleep duration, and time of last caloric intake as top predictors of visceral adipose tissue.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Health-Related Quality of Life in Paediatric Oncology: A Comparative Study with Non-Oncological Chronic Illness and Healthy Peers.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional study at Hong Kong Children's Hospital comparing children and adolescents with cancer, non-oncological chronic illness, and healthy peers found the poorest sleep quality in the oncology group (60.0% poor sleep, PSQI ≥5) and the lowest HRQoL. Across the full sample, poor sleep quality was independently associated with lower HRQoL after adjustment.

papers.title: Psychopharmacological advances in neurorehabilitation after traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes psychopharmacological evidence from the past 18 months for neuropsychiatric sequelae after traumatic brain injury and proposes a three-step approach: deprescribing recovery-limiting medications, characterizing individual symptoms, and selecting symptom-targeted treatments. Methylphenidate showed the most consistent evidence for attention and processing speed, while no treatment was established as disease-modifying.

papers.title: Sleep and Awake Bruxism and Mental Health Conditions: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of the 1982 Pelotas Birth Cohort.
papers.summary: In the 1982 Pelotas Birth Cohort, self-reported sleep and awake bruxism at age 40 were associated with female sex, alcohol dependence, and depression; participants with probable common mental disorders at both ages 30 and 40 had higher prevalence of awake bruxism (PR 2.02) and sleep bruxism (PR 1.52).

papers.title: Effects of Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction Combined With Perioperative Refined Nursing on Postoperative Sleep Disturbances, Anxiety, and Depression in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.summary: In a propensity-matched retrospective analysis of 146 CABG patients, adding mindfulness-based stress reduction to refined perioperative nursing was associated with lower postoperative anxiety and depression scores, better actigraphic sleep, lower IL-6, cortisol, and TNF-α, higher orexin, and shorter time to first ambulation.

papers.title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Comprehensive Nursing Care in Improving the Well-Being of Patients With Colon Cancer Who Developed Postoperative Sleep Disorders.
papers.summary: In a propensity-matched retrospective study of 104 colon cancer surgery patients with postoperative sleep disorders, comprehensive nursing care was associated with greater reductions in anxiety and depression scores, shorter recovery times, and better quality-of-life and sleep quality scores than routine nursing.

papers.title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns
papers.summary: The authors introduce LocPA, a computational framework using confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity networks, and local disease-enrichment testing, and apply it to UK Biobank accelerometry to identify low-activity and sleep-disrupted physical activity phenotypes enriched across six diseases, with replication in NHANES.

papers.title: Caring for the Caregivers: A Narrative Review of Physician Health Protection Across High-Income Countries and Lessons for Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on physician burnout, depression, suicide risk, and occupational health across high- and low- and middle-income countries, finding greater severity in LMICs due to weaker protections and limited mental health services, and proposes policy-oriented support strategies.

papers.title: Acetaminophen and chronic post-surgical neuropathic pain: a randomized double blind cross-over study.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 30 patients with chronic post-surgical peripheral neuropathic pain, 3 g/day oral acetaminophen was no better than placebo for 7-day mean pain intensity (effect size -0.09, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.26; P = 0.607) or any secondary outcome, with no observed adverse events.

papers.title: Respiratory health risks associated with humidifier disinfectant exposure in South Korea: A systematic review and meta-analysis with exposure-response evaluation.
papers.journal: Journal of exposure science & environmental epidemiology
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 South Korean observational studies found humidifier disinfectant exposure strongly associated with respiratory disease (pooled OR 7.02, 95% CI 1.97–24.98), with the strongest association for lung injury (pooled OR 94.53, 95% CI 61.31–145.73) and consistent exposure-response relationships across multiple exposure metrics.

papers.title: Substituting Hydromorphone for Morphine in Medical Aid in Dying: Clinical and Practice Implications.
papers.summary: This quasi-experimental pre-post study of 83 Medical Aid in Dying patients during a morphine shortage found median time to death did not differ between hydromorphone and morphine (55 vs 65.5 minutes; p = 0.29), while hydromorphone was associated with shorter median time to sleep (3 vs 5.5 minutes; adjusted HR 2.08, 95% CI 1.29–3.36).

papers.title: As Natural as Sleep: A Literature Study of Catholic Perspectives on Palliative Sedation.
papers.summary: Using a scoping review with Grounded Theory and argument-based literature analysis, this study mapped Catholic perspectives on palliative sedation, finding that it is welcomed as a means of alleviating suffering but subject to reservations about distinguishing it from deliberately ending life and about effects of impaired consciousness on patients' spiritual lives.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
